text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today as U.S. crude oil prices dropped nearly 8% for the week following diplomatic talks between Iran and the U.S. at the United Nations. When crude prices fall, oil companies' revenues and profits typically contract, putting downward pressure on their stock. The oil market's worry about a potential deal—or at least reduced geopolitical tension—outweighed the reality that Saudi Arabia is actually ramping up exports despite regional turmoil.

The two-week decline of 7.3% reflects a broader shift in investor thinking about oil supply risk. Even though Middle Eastern infrastructure is under attack and threats remain real, the prospect of U.S.-Iran negotiations has eased some of the supply-shock premium that had been baked into prices. For an oil company, lower prices mean lower margins, which is why the stock has tracked the commodity weakness even as global crude (trading at $114.89) remains well above U.S. crude ($96.41).
